vocab.definition: making progress as planned and likely to succeed on time

vocab.definition: an important stage or event in the progress of a project

vocab.definition: a problem that stops work from moving forward until someone solves it

vocab.definition: to make a new product or service available, often in stages

vocab.definition: to give official approval for something

vocab.definition: to contact someone again or take further action about something

vocab.example_zh: 我明天早上會再跟供應商追蹤一下。

vocab.example_zh: 儀表板讓人一眼就看出團隊進度。

reading.title: The Status Update Nobody Skips
paragraphs: Every Friday afternoon, thousands of managers open a pile of weekly status updates, and most of them stop reading after the first few lines. The problem is rarely a lack of information. It is that the important news is buried under a long list of meetings and small tasks.

A good update lets the reader see the situation at a glance. Start with one sentence on the overall picture: is the project on track, at risk, or behind? Then list what has changed since last week. Here, grammar quietly helps you. "We have finished the payment flow" tells the reader the result matters now. "We finished the payment flow on Tuesday" simply reports a past event with a time. Choose the first form for your achievements and the second when the date itself is useful.

Next, be honest about blockers. If legal hasn't signed off on the new terms, say so, and say who needs to act. Managers would much rather hear about a problem on Friday than discover it at a launch meeting. Mention any milestone you have reached, and name any work that will carry over to next week, so nothing silently disappears.
Finally, finish with clear next steps: what you plan to roll out, who you will follow up with, and what you need from the reader. Three short sections, a few bullet points each, are usually enough.
Writing like this takes ten extra minutes. In return, your manager understands your project in thirty seconds, and that makes your work far more visible.

questions.q: According to the article, why do managers often stop reading status updates?
options: The updates contain too little information.
The important news is hidden under less important details.
The updates arrive too late in the week.
Managers prefer to get updates in meetings.
questions.explain_zh: 第一段：the important news is buried under a long list of meetings and small tasks，重點被埋在一堆瑣事裡。

questions.q: When does the writer suggest using the past simple?
options: When you want to show that a result matters now
When you describe a blocker
When the specific time of the event is useful
When you write the first sentence of the update
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：Choose ... the second (過去式) when the date itself is useful，日期本身有意義時用過去式。

questions.q: What can we infer about the writer's view of reporting problems?
options: Reporting problems early builds trust with managers.
Problems should only be reported once they are solved.
Blockers are best discussed at launch meetings.
Managers usually ignore problems in written updates.
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：主管 would much rather hear about a problem on Friday than discover it at a launch meeting。作者暗示提早說比較好，這題考推論。

grammar.point_zh: 現在完成式 vs 過去簡單式
grammar.explain_zh: 現在完成式（have/has + p.p.）強調「到現在的結果或經驗」，不講明確的過去時間，常搭配 already、yet、so far、this week。過去簡單式講「過去某個時間點已經結束的事」，常搭配 yesterday、last week、on Tuesday、in 2023。進度報告裡，說成果用現在完成式（We've finished…），講什麼時候發生用過去式（We finished it on Tuesday）。注意：有 yesterday、last week 這類明確過去時間時，不能用現在完成式。
grammar.pattern: have/has + p.p.（結果、到目前為止） ／ V-ed + 明確過去時間（last week, on Monday）

examples.en: We've completed three of the five milestones so far.
examples.zh: 到目前為止我們完成了五個里程碑中的三個。

examples.en: We completed the second milestone last Thursday.
examples.zh: 我們上週四完成了第二個里程碑。

examples.en: Has the client signed off on the design yet?

exercises.q: We ___ the new dashboard to all users last Monday.
options: have rolled out
rolled out
have been rolling out
roll out
exercises.explain_zh: 有明確過去時間 last Monday，要用過去簡單式 rolled out。

exercises.q: So far this week, we ___ (fix) twelve bugs.
exercises.explain_zh: So far this week（到目前為止）表示期間還沒結束，用現在完成式 have fixed。

options: I have sent the report yesterday.
I sent the report yesterday.
I have send the report yesterday.
I was sent the report yesterday by me.
exercises.explain_zh: yesterday 是明確過去時間，不能和現在完成式連用，所以是 I sent the report yesterday。

exercises.q: Legal still ___ (not / sign) off on the contract, so we can't start.
exercises.explain_zh: still … not 表示到現在還沒發生，主詞 Legal 視為單數，用 hasn't signed。

exercises.q: A: "When did you finish the migration?" B: "We ___ it on Wednesday night."
options: have finished
finished
have been finishing
had been finished
exercises.explain_zh: 問句用 When did…，問的是過去的時間點，回答也用過去式 finished。

listening.title: Kevin checks in on the weekly update

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Hi Grace, I just read your status update. Thanks, it was really easy to follow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Oh good. I tried to keep it short so you could see everything at a glance.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: It worked. So the booking feature is still on track for the end of the month?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Yes. We've finished the search page, and we reached the testing milestone on Wednesday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Great. You mentioned one blocker, though. What's going on with the payment provider?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Their legal team hasn't signed off on the contract yet. Until they do, we can't connect to the live system.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Have you followed up with them?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: I emailed them on Monday and called yesterday. They promised an answer by Thursday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Okay. If nothing comes back by then, let me know and I'll call their director.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Thanks, that would help. Otherwise, the refund screens will carry over to next week, but we can still roll out the rest on time.

questions.q: What did the team do on Wednesday?
options: They finished the search page.
They reached the testing milestone.
They signed the contract.
They launched the booking feature.
questions.explain_zh: Grace：we reached the testing milestone on Wednesday。搜尋頁是「已完成」，沒有說哪天。

questions.q: Why can't the team connect to the payment provider's live system?
options: The provider's legal team hasn't approved the contract.
The provider's system is down.
Kevin hasn't approved the budget.
The search page isn't finished.
questions.explain_zh: Their legal team hasn't signed off on the contract yet. Until they do, we can't connect…

questions.q: What will Kevin do if there is no answer by Thursday?
options: Cancel the contract
Move the launch date
Call the provider's director
Remove the refund screens
questions.explain_zh: Kevin：If nothing comes back by then, let me know and I'll call their director.

dictation: We've finished the search page, and we reached the testing milestone on Wednesday.
Their legal team hasn't signed off on the contract yet.
I emailed them on Monday and called yesterday.

shadowing: Overall, the project is on track for the end of the month.
We've finished the search page, and testing started on Wednesday.
Our main blocker is that legal hasn't signed off on the contract yet.
I'll follow up with them on Thursday and keep you posted.

prompts.question: Give your manager a 30-second spoken update on a project you're working on. What have you finished, and what happened this week?
prompts.question_zh: 用 30 秒口頭向主管報告你手上的專案：已經完成了什麼？這週發生了什麼事？
hints: Overall picture: Overall, we're on track / a bit behind…
Past events with a time: On Tuesday, we…
prompts.sample: Overall, we're on track. We've already finished the new login page and most of the account settings. On Tuesday, we ran the first round of user tests, and people found it much easier to use. The only blocker is that we haven't received the final icons from the design agency, so I'll follow up with them tomorrow.

prompts.question: Have you ever had a project where something blocked your progress? What happened, and what did you do?
prompts.question_zh: 你有沒有遇過專案被某件事卡住的經驗？發生了什麼？你怎麼處理？
hints: Experience: I've had that a few times…
Story in the past: Last year, we were waiting for…
Action: So I followed up with…
prompts.sample: Yes, I've had that a few times. Last year, we were waiting for our IT department to set up a new server, and for two weeks nothing happened. In the end I booked a short meeting with their manager, explained exactly what we needed, and we got it the next day. Since then, I've always flagged blockers in my weekly update.

writing.task: Write a weekly status update email to your manager, Sarah, about a project you're working on (real or imagined). Give the overall status, what has been done, one blocker, and next week's plan. Use both the present perfect and the past simple correctly.
writing.task_zh: 寫一封每週進度報告 email 給主管 Sarah，內容是你正在做的專案（真實或虛構皆可）：整體狀態、已完成的事、一個卡關點、下週計畫。正確使用現在完成式和過去簡單式。
writing.sample:
Subject: Weekly update – customer portal (Week 44)

Hi Sarah,

Overall, the customer portal is on track for the December launch.

Done this week:
- We've finished the account and billing pages.
- We ran the first usability test on Tuesday with eight customers, and so far the feedback has been very positive.

Blocker:
- IT hasn't given us access to the production server yet. I asked them on Monday and will follow up again tomorrow. If it isn't sorted by Wednesday, the deployment work will carry over to the following week.

Next week:
- Fix the issues from the usability test
- Start the data migration

Let me know if you have any questions.

Best,
Vincent
checklist_zh: 第一句就說整體狀態（on track / at risk / behind）
成果用現在完成式（We've finished…），有明確時間的事用過去式（on Tuesday）
有 yesterday、last week 的句子不要用 have + p.p.
卡關點要說清楚誰要處理、你會怎麼追蹤
用條列分段，讓主管一眼看懂

translation.zh: 整體來說，這個專案仍按計畫進行。
translation.en: Overall, the project is still on track.
alt: Overall, the project is still on schedule.

translation.zh: 我們已經完成了付款流程。
alt: We have completed the payment flow.

translation.zh: 我們上週二推出了新版本。
translation.en: We rolled out the new version last Tuesday.
alt: We released the new version last Tuesday.

translation.zh: 法務還沒核准合約，這是我們目前最大的卡關點。
translation.en: Legal hasn't signed off on the contract yet, and that's our biggest blocker right now.
alt: Legal hasn't approved the contract yet, which is our biggest blocker at the moment.

translation.zh: 退款頁面會順延到下週，我明天會再跟供應商追蹤。
translation.en: The refund pages will carry over to next week, and I'll follow up with the vendor tomorrow.
alt: The refund pages will be carried over to next week. I'll follow up with the supplier tomorrow.

reading.title: When Green Turns Red Overnight
paragraphs: Anyone who has worked on a large project has seen it happen. For weeks, every status report shows a reassuring green light. Then, a fortnight before launch, the project suddenly turns red, and everyone asks the same question: how did nobody see this coming?

The uncomfortable answer is that someone usually did. Somewhere on the team, a developer noticed that an integration was harder than expected, or a designer realised that the requirements had shifted. But the signal got watered down on its way up. Each layer of reporting smoothed the edges a little, because nobody wanted to be the one who cried wolf, and "slightly behind" quietly became "on track".

Experienced project leads call this the watermelon effect: green on the outside, red on the inside. It thrives in cultures where bad news is treated as a personal failure rather than as useful information. If the last person who raised a risk was grilled in front of senior management, people learn to keep their heads down.

Fixing it is less about better templates and more about trust. Some teams add an "amber" status that people are explicitly encouraged to use, so there is a respectable middle ground between everything being fine and everything being on fire. Others ask a sharper question in every update: "What has changed since last week that worries you?" That wording makes it normal to admit uncertainty before it hardens into a crisis.

Leaders set the tone here. When a manager responds to an early warning with "Thanks for flagging it, what do you need?" instead of "Why is this late?", the next warning tends to arrive sooner. Over time, the reports stop being a performance and start being a genuine early-warning system.

questions.q: According to the article, why do projects often seem to turn red suddenly?
options: Problems are usually impossible to predict.
Warnings are softened as they move up through the organization.
Developers rarely notice technical problems.
Senior managers ignore detailed reports.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：the signal got watered down on its way up. Each layer of reporting smoothed the edges，警訊一層層往上報時被淡化了。

options: A project that looks healthy in reports but is actually in trouble
A project that grows larger than planned
A team that changes its status colors too often
A manager who reports problems too early
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：green on the outside, red on the inside，外表看起來沒問題，裡面其實有大問題。

questions.q: What can we infer about a person who was "grilled in front of senior management"?
options: They were praised for their honesty.
They were promoted after raising the risk.
They were harshly questioned, which discouraged others from speaking up.
They were asked to write a new status template.
questions.explain_zh: grill 在這裡是「嚴厲質問」。下一句 people learn to keep their heads down 暗示這讓其他人不敢再提風險，這題考推論。

questions.q: Why does the writer recommend asking "What has changed since last week that worries you?"
options: It shortens the status meeting.
It makes admitting uncertainty feel normal.
It replaces the need for a status color.
It helps managers assign blame more quickly.
questions.explain_zh: 第四段：That wording makes it normal to admit uncertainty before it hardens into a crisis。

listening.title: Is the project really green?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Linda
lines.text: Marcus, got a sec? I was looking at your update, and it's green across the board again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Yeah, things have been going pretty smoothly, actually.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Linda
lines.text: Okay, but I bumped into Priya in the kitchen, and she said the data import has been a nightmare all week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Ah. Well, it's been, um, a bit bumpy. But we've got a workaround, so I didn't think it was worth worrying you about.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Linda
lines.text: Look, I'd honestly rather hear about the bumps. How solid is the workaround?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: It's fine for the test data. With the full customer database, though, it might take, I don't know, ten hours instead of one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Linda
lines.text: Ten hours? We've only got a four-hour window on launch night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Right. Yeah, when you put it like that, it's probably amber, not green.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Linda
lines.text: No harm done, we've still got three weeks. What do you need to sort it out?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Honestly? A database specialist for a few days. Priya's been carrying this on her own.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Linda
lines.text: Leave it with me. I'll ask Tom if we can borrow someone from his team, and let's mark it amber in Friday's report.

questions.q: How did Linda find out about the problem with the data import?
options: From Marcus's status update
From a conversation with Priya
From an email from Tom
From the test results
questions.explain_zh: Linda：I bumped into Priya in the kitchen, and she said the data import has been a nightmare all week.

questions.q: Why is the workaround a serious risk?
options: It doesn't work with test data.
It could take much longer than the time available on launch night.
Priya doesn't know how to use it.
It would delete customer data.
questions.explain_zh: 完整資料可能要 ten hours，但上線當晚 only got a four-hour window。

questions.q: What can we infer about Marcus's original status report?
options: He deliberately lied to Linda.
He made the situation look better than it really was.
He reported the problem but Linda missed it.
He had not spoken to his team for weeks.
questions.explain_zh: Marcus 承認 it's probably amber, not green，原本報告把狀況講得比實際好，但他說是 didn't think it was worth worrying you，不是故意說謊。這題考推論。

dictation: I'd honestly rather hear about the bumps.
We've only got a four-hour window on launch night.
Priya's been carrying this on her own.

glossary.zh: 喊「狼來了」、虛報警訊（cry wolf 的過去式）
glossary.definition: to warn people about a danger that is not real, so they stop believing you
made weaker or less strong than it was originally
to ask someone a lot of difficult questions in an unfriendly way
in status reports, a warning level between green (fine) and red (in trouble)
a way of getting around a problem without actually fixing it
